newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds look ahead to Suedwest, Petronas in dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds look ahead to Suedwest, Petronas in dlrs.

text.p: Primary market issuance dwindled to a halt on Friday afternoon, as the market digested the release of the U.S. September non-farm payrolls data and focused its attention on next week's supply.
"The market is in great shape, we've seen lots of demand for dollar paper today from across-the board," a syndicate manager said.

New issues traders said they were awaiting the launch of Suedwest LB's $500 million five-year Eurobond via CS First Boston and Goldman Sachs next week. Market speculation is for a spread of 15 to 17 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
A syndicate official close to Suedwest's bond said demand was likely to come from the "traditional dollar-investor base".
"There'll be good Asian, U.K. and Swiss demand," he said.

Also in dollars, from the emerging market sector, Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) is expected to launch a $1.0 billion global bond late next week setting a benchmark for both Malaysian credits and the Asian region.

Petronas -- Malaysia's national oil company -- was likely to issue the bonds in two tranches with five- and 10-year maturities, dealers said. "It will put the whole region into a positive light," a syndicate manager close to the deal said.

From Latin America, the market is still awaiting the launch of Brazil's debut in the global bond market -- a $750 million five-or 10-year bond. There is very little Brazilian sovereign paper outstanding in the Eurobond market, and no emerging market 10-year dollar bonds. Thus spreads are expected to be as tight as 220 b.p. to 250 b.p. for five years and 320 b.p. to 350 b.p. for 10 years. It is possible the proceeds of the bond could be used to buy back Brady bonds, sources have said.
While Colombia is due to tap the mark sector with a 300 million mark five-year FRN via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Merrill Lynch.
Also, Petroleo Brasileiro SA -- the Brazilian state oil company Petrobras -- will launch a $250 million Eurobond next week, sources close to the deal said on Friday.
The bond is expected to be issued in two tranches -- one maturing after five years with an expected spread of 250 to 270 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
The other is expected to mature after 10 years with talk of a 340 to 360 b.p. spread.
Each bond is expected to be for $125 million.
Chase Manhattan International is the sold lead manager for the transaction.
In the sterling sector, Annington Homes is expected to launch three bonds backed by rental payments from the Ministry of Defence for a total of 863 million stg via HSBC and Nomura next week.
A 330 million stg FRN with a five-year average life, a 173 million stg fixed-rate bond with a 12.5-year average life and a 360 million stg fixed-rate bond with a 20-year average life.
Meanwhile roadshows for NatWest's $5.0 billion securitisation of syndicated loans made to corporates start on Monday.
